probes.query: Which Sinatra method lets a route immediately stop and return a response, and how is it implemented?
expectedFacts: Base#halt (base.rb:1028) immediately stops a request by calling throw :halt with the given response
probes.author: ruby-author
probes.notes: Verified: grep -n '^    def halt' lib/sinatra/base.rb -> base.rb:1028. Body: `throw :halt, response`.

probes.query: Where does Sinatra match an incoming HTTP request against the registered routes and run the matching block? Looking for the get/post route matching logic.
expectedFacts: Base#route! (base.rb:1064) iterates base.routes for the request method and process_route (base.rb:1098) tests the Mustermann pattern against @request.path_info and runs the block; the get/post DSL methods (class << self, base.rb:1531/1776) only DEFINE routes, they do not match incoming requests
probes.author: ruby-author
probes.notes: DISTRACTOR: surface tokens 'get/post route' point to the route-DEFINITION DSL (def get @1531, def route @1776 inside `class << self`), but the gold for matching INCOMING requests is the instance methods route! and process_route. Verified: grep -n '^    def route!\|^    def process_route\|^      def get\b\|^      def route\b' lib/sinatra/base.rb -> route!@1064, process_route@1098, get@1531, route@1776. process_route matches `pattern.params(@request.path_info)`.

probes.query: In classic top-level Sinatra style, calling get '/' at the file scope works without subclassing. How do those bare get/post calls reach the application class? Trace the delegation.
expectedFacts: main.rb does `extend Sinatra::Delegator` (main.rb:52); Delegator.delegate defines forwarding methods (base.rb:2101) that send to Delegator.target, which is set to Application (base.rb:2126)
probes.author: ruby-author
probes.notes: Verified: grep -n 'extend Sinatra::Delegator' lib/sinatra/main.rb -> main.rb:52. grep -n '^  module Delegator\|self.target = Application' lib/sinatra/base.rb -> module Delegator@2101, self.target = Application@2126. Delegator.delegate (base.rb:2102) define_method forwards to Delegator.target.send (base.rb:2109).

probes.query: We are writing a Sinatra extension. What is the mechanism that registers an extension onto an app, and what callback (if any) does the extension receive when it is registered?
expectedFacts: The class-level register method (base.rb:1564) appends extensions, extends the app with each, and calls extension.registered(self) (base.rb:1569) if the extension defines a `registered` hook
probes.author: ruby-author
probes.notes: Verified: grep -n '^      def register\b\|extension.registered\|^      def helpers\b' lib/sinatra/base.rb -> helpers@1557, register@1564, `extension.registered(self) if extension.respond_to?(:registered)`@1569. Note: Application.register (base.rb:2090) also overrides to delegate added public instance methods (a tempting distractor branch).

probes.query: What is the order of operations Sinatra runs when handling a single request: before filters, static files, the route, after filters, and exception handling? Point me at the orchestrating method.
expectedFacts: dispatch! (base.rb:1181) runs static! then the :before filter then route! inside invoke, rescues exceptions via handle_exception!, and runs the :after filter in an ensure block
probes.author: ruby-author
probes.notes: Verified: grep -n '^    def dispatch!' lib/sinatra/base.rb -> base.rb:1181. Body calls static! / filter! :before / route! inside invoke, rescue ::Exception -> handle_exception!, ensure -> filter! :after.

probes.query: When a route sets the response content type, how does Sinatra decide whether to append a charset parameter to the Content-Type header?
expectedFacts: Helpers#content_type (base.rb:384) appends charset (settings.default_encoding) only when params has no :charset, the mime type matches settings.add_charset, and the mime type does not already include 'charset'
probes.author: ruby-author
probes.notes: Verified: grep -n '^    def content_type' lib/sinatra/base.rb -> base.rb:384. Body checks `unless params.include?(:charset) || settings.add_charset.all? { |p| !(p === mime_type) }` then `params.delete :charset if mime_type.include? 'charset'`.

probes.query: Find the Rack wrapper class Sinatra defines as a Struct that handles async EventMachine responses.
expectedFacts: ExtendedRack is declared as `class ExtendedRack < Struct.new(:app)` (base.rb:225) and its call method handles env['async.callback'] for async (EventMachine) responses
probes.author: ruby-author
probes.notes: Verified: grep -n 'class ExtendedRack < Struct.new' lib/sinatra/base.rb -> base.rb:225 (`class ExtendedRack < Struct.new(:app)`). #call inspects env['async.callback'] and after_response uses EventMachine.next_tick.

probes.query: Where in the Sinatra core library is the database/ORM layer (ActiveRecord-style models, establish_connection, has_many/belongs_to associations)?
probes.author: ruby-author
probes.notes: Verified ABSENT: grep -rniE 'ActiveRecord|establish_connection|has_many|belongs_to' lib/ -> 0 results (exit 1). Sinatra is a routing/DSL framework with no built-in ORM or database layer.

probes.query: How do you register a custom MIME type extension mapping in Sinatra (e.g. mapping :json to application/json), and where is that registration stored?
expectedFacts: The class-level mime_type(type, value) method (base.rb:1459) writes Rack::Mime::MIME_TYPES[".#{type}"] = value when a value is given; the Helpers#mime_type instance method (base.rb:378) only delegates to Base.mime_type for lookups
probes.author: ruby-author
probes.notes: Verified: grep -n '^      def mime_type\b\|^    def mime_type\b' lib/sinatra/base.rb -> Helpers#mime_type@378 (lookup only: `Base.mime_type(type)`), class<<self mime_type@1459 (registrar: `Rack::Mime::MIME_TYPES[type] = value`).
